question.prompt: A model used to estimate the time it will take to hike to the top of the mountain on a trail is of the form \(T = aL + bG,\) where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants, \(T\) is the time in minutes, \(L\) is the length of the trail in miles, and \(G\) is the altitude gain in feet. The model estimates that it will take \(69\) minutes to hike to the top if a trail is \(1.5\) miles long and ascends \(800\) feet, as well as if a trail is \(1.2\) miles long and ascends \(1100\) feet. How many minutes does the model estimate it will take to hike to the top if the trail is \(4.2\) miles long and ascends \(4000\) feet?

solutions.title: Subtract and substitute
solutions.explanation:
Both known hikes take \(69\) minutes, so subtracting their model equations gives a useful relation between \(a\) and \(b\). The data give
\[
\begin{aligned}
1.5a+800b&=69,\\
1.2a+1100b&=69.
\end{aligned}
\]
Subtracting the second equation from the first yields
\[
0.3a-300b=0,
\qquad a=1000b.
\]
Substitute this into the first equation:
\[
1.5(1000b)+800b=69,
\]
so \(2300b=69\), giving \(b=0.03\) and \(a=30\).

Thus the model is \(T=30L+0.03G\). For the requested hike,
\[
T=30(4.2)+0.03(4000)=126+120=246.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{246}\) minutes, choice \(\text{B}\).
